questions.text: As per the thermodynamic data in the table, for a reaction at 298 K with ΔH = –50 kJ mol−1 and ΔS = –100 J mol−1 K−1, the reaction is spontaneous in which temperature range?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For ΔH<0 and ΔS<0, ΔG = ΔH – TΔS is negative only when T < ΔH/ΔS; here ΔH/ΔS = (–50,000 J)/(–100 J K−1) = 500 K, so spontaneity occurs below 500 K. Full solution: Calculate ΔG = –50,000 – T(–100) = –50,000 + 100T. Set ΔG<0 → 100T < 50,000 → T < 500 K.

Shortcut: Use the Maclaurin expansion e^x = 1 + x + x^2/2 + x^3/6 + ... Then numerator ≈ x^2/2, so limit = 1/2. Full solution: Apply L'Hospital's rule twice: first derivative gives (e^x -1)/(2x), still 0/0; second derivative gives e^x/2 → 1/2 as x→0.

questions.text: Light of wavelength λ is incident on a photosensitive metal surface with work function φ₀. The stopping potential is measured to be V₀. If the wavelength of the incident light is changed to λ/2 (assuming λ < hc/φ₀), the new stopping potential becomes:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation eV₀ = hc/λ - φ₀. For λ/2, eV₀' = 2hc/λ - φ₀ = (hc/λ - φ₀) + hc/λ = eV₀ + hc/λ. Thus V₀' = V₀ + hc/(eλ). Full Solution: For first case, eV₀ = hc/λ - φ₀. For second case (λ' = λ/2), eV₀' = hc/(λ/2) - φ₀ = 2hc/λ - φ₀. Substitute φ₀ = hc/λ - eV₀ from first equation: eV₀' = 2hc/λ - (hc/λ - eV₀) = hc/λ + eV₀. Therefore V₀' = V₀ + hc/(eλ).

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment (YDSE), the fringe width is β. A transparent glass slab of thickness t and refractive index μ is introduced in the path of one of the beams. The central bright fringe shifts to a position originally occupied by the n-th bright fringe. The value of n is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Optical path difference introduced by slab = (μ - 1)t. Number of fringes shifted n = (Path difference) / λ = (μ - 1)t/λ. Full Solution: Introduction of a slab of thickness t and refractive index μ in one path increases the optical path length by (μ - 1)t compared to air. For the central bright fringe (zero path difference) to appear at the new position, the geometrical path difference must compensate this. The shift corresponds to n fringes where nλ = (μ - 1)t. Hence n = (μ - 1)t/λ. Note: Fringe width β = λD/d is not needed for n.

questions.text: As per the table below, which element has the highest first ionization energy?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Across a period, first ionization energy generally increases, but there is a dip at Group 13 (Al) due to removal of a p-electron; thus Si (Group 14) has the highest IE among the given elements. Full solution: The table shows IE values: Na=496, Mg=738, Al=578, Si=786 kJ/mol. Comparing these, Si has the maximum value.

questions.text: If ω is a complex cube root of unity, then the value of (1 - ω + ω²)⁵ + (1 - ω² + ω)⁵ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use 1+ω+ω²=0 ⇒ 1-ω+ω² = -2ω and 1-ω²+ω = -2ω². The expression becomes (-2ω)⁵ + (-2ω²)⁵ = -32(ω⁵+ω¹⁰) = -32(ω²+ω) = -32(-1) = 32. Full: Since ω³=1 and ω≠1, we have 1+ω+ω²=0. Thus 1-ω+ω² = -2ω and 1+ω-ω² = -2ω². Raising to power 5 and summing gives -32(ω⁵+ω¹⁰) = -32(ω²+ω) = 32.

questions.text: As per the defect data in the table, why does the density of a crystal decrease in a Schottky defect?

options.label: C
options.text: Equal number of cations and anions are missing from lattice sites

options.label: D
options.text: Electrons are trapped in anion vacancies

questions.solution: Shortcut: Schottky defect is a stoichiometric pair of cation and anion vacancies; mass decreases while volume remains nearly constant, lowering density. Full solution: In Schottky defect, equal numbers of cations and anions leave their lattice sites creating vacancies, reducing the total mass in the crystal without a proportional volume change, hence density drops. Frenkel defects involve interstitial displacement, not mass loss.

As per the data in the table, the complex [Ni(CN)4]2− is square planar and diamagnetic. What is the hybridization of the Ni centre?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Square planar geometry for d8 metal ions (Ni2+) arises from dsp2 hybridization; other hybridizations correspond to tetrahedral (sp3), trigonal bipyramidal (sp3d), or octahedral (d2sp3). Full solution: Ni2+ is d8; in a strong field CN− ligand, the complex is low-spin square planar, requiring dsp2 hybridization to accommodate four ligand pairs in the plane.

questions.text: A solid sphere, a hollow sphere, and a uniform disc, all having identical mass Mand radius R, are released from rest at the top of an identical rough inclined plane. Which object reaches the bottom first?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Acceleration a = g sinθ / (1 + I/MR²). Smaller I/MR² gives larger 'a'. Ratios: Solid (2/5=0.4), Disc (1/2=0.5), Hollow (2/3≈0.67). Solid sphere has smallest ratio, hence highest acceleration. Full Solution: For rolling without slipping, a = g sinθ / (1 + k²/R²) where k is radius of gyration. Solid sphere: k²/R² = 2/5 ⇒ a = 5/7 g sinθ. Disc: k²/R² = 1/2 ⇒ a = 2/3 g sinθ. Hollow sphere: k²/R² = 2/3 ⇒ a = 3/5 g sinθ. Since 5/7 > 2/3 > 3/5, the solid sphere accelerates fastest and reaches first.

questions.text: As per the table of aromatic substrates, which compound undergoes nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) most readily?
questions.solution: Shortcut: SNAr requires a strong electron‑withdrawing group ortho/para to the leaving group; 2,4‑dinitrochlorobenzene has two nitro groups activating the ring, whereas the others lack such activation or a leaving group. Full solution: Chlorobenzene and bromobenzene are unactivated; nitrobenzene has no halogen leaving group. Only 2,4‑dinitrochlorobenzene meets both criteria.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C₀ is charged to charge Q₀ and disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant K is slowly inserted between the plates completely filling the gap. The work done by the external agent during this process is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For an isolated capacitor (Q constant), energy U = Q²/(2C). Initial Uᵢ = Q₀²/(2C₀). Final U_f = Q₀²/(2KC₀). Work done by external agent W_ext = ΔU = U_f - Uᵢ = Q₀²/(2C₀)(1/K - 1). The negative sign indicates the agent works against the attractive force. Full Solution: Since the battery is disconnected, charge Q₀ remains constant. Capacitance becomes KC₀. Initial energy Uᵢ = Q₀²/(2C₀). Final energy U_f = Q₀²/(2KC₀). By work-energy theorem, work done by external agent equals change in stored energy: W_ext = U_f - Uᵢ = Q₀²/(2C₀)(1/K - 1).

questions.text: If sinθ + cosθ = 1/2, then the value of sin2θ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Square both sides: (sinθ+cosθ)^2 = sin^2θ+cos^2θ+2sinθcosθ = 1+sin2θ = 1/4 → sin2θ = -3/4. Full solution: (1/2)^2 = 1/4 = 1 + sin2θ ⇒ sin2θ = 1/4 - 1 = -3/4.

questions.text: An on-conducting thin ring of radius R carries a total charge q uniformly distributed over its circumference. The ring is rotated about its axis with a constant angular velocity ω. The magnetic moment of the rotating ring is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Equivalent current I = Charge / Time Period = q / (2π/ω) = qω/(2π). Magnetic moment μ = I × Area = (qω/(2π)) × πR² = qωR²/2. Full Solution: The rotating charge constitutes a current loop. Current I = q/T = qω/(2π). Area of the loop A = πR². Magnetic moment M = I × A = (qω/(2π)) × πR² = ½ qωR². Direction is along the axis given by right-hand rule.
questions.topic: Magnetism - Magnetic Moment of Rotating Charge

questions.text: If ω is an on-real cube root of unity, then the value of (1 - ω + ω²)⁴ + (1 + ω - ω²)⁴ is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use 1+ω+ω²=0 ⇒ 1+ω²=-ω and 1+ω=-ω². Then (1-ω+ω²)=-2ω and (1+ω-ω²)=-2ω². The expression becomes 16ω⁴+16ω⁸=16(ω+ω²)=16(-1)=-16. Full Solution: Since ω³=1 and 1+ω+ω²=0, we have 1+ω²=-ω and 1+ω=-ω². First bracket: (1+ω²)-ω = -ω-ω = -2ω. Second bracket: (1+ω)-ω² = -ω²-ω² = -2ω². Raising to power 4: (-2ω)⁴ + (-2ω²)⁴ = 16ω⁴ + 16ω⁸ = 16ω + 16ω² = 16(ω+ω²) = -16.
